covered_actors: Providers of general-purpose AI models (within the Union and in third countries placing models on the Union market)
Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
Downstream modifiers of general-purpose AI models exceeding modification compute thresholds
Downstream providers integrating general-purpose AI models into AI systems
Authorised representatives established in the Union for third-country providers
Providers of general-purpose AI models released under free and open-source licences
compliance_deadlines: 2025-08-02: Entry into application of Chapter V AI Act obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models (Article 113(b) AI Act) and Commission Article 52 designation/contest decisions.

Within two weeks after meeting or foreseeing the systemic-risk threshold (or within two weeks after 2025-08-02 for models trained or planned for placement after that date): Mandatory notification to the Commission under Article 52(1) AI Act.
2026-08-02: Entry into application of Commission enforcement powers and fines under Article 101 AI Act.
2027-08-02: Compliance deadline for general-purpose AI models placed on the market before 2025-08-02 (Article 111(3) AI Act).
penalties_summary: Starting on 2 August 2026, the European Commission may impose fines of up to 3% of global annual turnover or EUR 15 million, whichever is higher (Article 101 AI Act), including for failure to notify systemic-risk classification. The Commission may also request information (Article 91), conduct model evaluations (Article 92), and order mitigation measures or recall models from the market (Article 93). Adherence to a code of practice assessed as adequate may serve as a mitigating factor when fixing fines.
implementation_notes: Non-binding interpretive guidelines adopted under Article 96(1) AI Act setting out the European Commission's enforcement interpretation for Chapter V GPAI obligations (subject to authoritative interpretation by the CJEU). Establishes indicative training-compute criteria (>10^23 FLOP with language, text-to-image, or text-to-video generation for GPAI models; >10^25 FLOP cumulative compute for systemic-risk presumption; >1/3 of original training compute for downstream modifiers), defines open-source exemption boundaries (requiring no monetisation and excluding systemic-risk models while maintaining copyright policy and training-data summary obligations), clarifies the compliance role of adequate codes of practice and harmonised standards, and outlines a collaborative, staged enforcement approach by the AI Office without requiring retraining or unlearning of pre-2 August 2025 models where impossible or disproportionate.
